verdict.rationale: React documents hydration of server-rendered HTML via hydrateRoot and server-side streaming that progressively fills in content before JavaScript loads. However, the pack never explicitly documents progressive or selective hydration, meaning parts of the page becoming interactive incrementally. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of progressive/selective hydration (e.g., Suspense-boundary hydration ordering), evidence of faster time-to-interactive, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can hydrate my server-rendered app progressively so pages become interactive faster

citations.quote: Call `hydrateRoot` to “attach” React to existing HTML that was already rendered by React in a server environment.
hydrateRoot lets you display React components inside a browser DOM node whose HTML content was previously generated by react-dom/server.
On the server, React lets you start streaming HTML while you’re still fetching data, progressively filling in the remaining content before any JavaScript code loads.
